DeSaulnier voted No on successive Israel aid bills through 2025–26, voted Yes on the Massie amendment eliminating $3.3B in military aid, sponsors the Block the Bombs Act, and stated in July 2025 he no longer votes for offensive military aid to Israel. CAIR Action endorsed him; Vote for Peace rated him an Ally. Earlier Yes votes on UNRWA cuts, a PLO entry ban, and the Boulder resolution, along with his non-sponsorship of genocide-recognition, complicate the record.

Joyce explicitly calls Gaza a genocide, identifies Netanyahu as a war criminal, refuses all Pro-Israel PAC money, and proposes AIPAC register under FARA. Her documented position frames the crisis around Netanyahu and the current government, and her FARA proposal targets AIPAC's lobbying rather than the US military relationship with Israel. Her insistence that Palestine should be free and her refusal of pro-another-country PAC funds place her well outside mainstream Democratic posture.

Simon sponsors the Block the Bombs Act and a resolution recognizing genocide of Palestinians in Gaza, issued a House press release calling for its end, and rejects AIPAC, DMFI, and Lockheed Martin funding. Track AIPAC and CAIR Action endorse her; Vote for Peace rates her an Ally. She voted for the Massie amendment eliminating $3.3 billion in Israel military aid but also for the Boulder resolution conflating anti-Zionism with antisemitic violence and against cutting $500 million for Israeli missile defense.

Wahab answered 'Yes' when directly asked about Gaza genocide at an April 2026 forum, introduced a California Senate resolution calling the conflict a genocide and demanding its end, and cosponsored the Block the Bombs Act. She has not separately sponsored genocide-recognition or UNRWA-restoration bills.

At an April 2026 Indivisible Tri-Valley forum, she declined to label Israel's Gaza actions as genocide, diverging from fellow candidates and the Alameda County Democratic Party.
